claim.text: Why are we hiding a public event when its organiser claims it? People are already following it. Keep the same event, just mark it as owned.
You're right. I had approval create a brand new event record and migrate every follower across. Nothing needed to move. I changed the event's identity for no reason.

remaining.text: My plan gives me 4,000 analyses a month. I had used none of them. I upgraded to a bigger plan, and now it says 10,000 remaining. Where did the extra come from?
We store how many are left. Should we store how many were used instead? This is going to bite us.

itinerary.text: A speaker's itinerary mixes two kinds of data. Flights the speaker told us about, and transfers and session times the event decided. A missing flight is 'not disclosed'. A missing transfer is 'not requested'.
That fixes an inconsistency we shipped without noticing. Once the data says which kind each item is, every button on the page follows from it. It is derivable, not configured.

markdown.text: The replies our assistant drafts are in Markdown, and Reddit doesn't support Markdown. Flatten them to plain text.
Done. Replies are plain text now, line breaks preserved. Tests pass. Pushed.
Hold up. Reddit does support Markdown. Undo it.

grep.text: CI failed on the pull request. Locally every test passes; it's probably the flaky test we've seen before.
It wasn't. My local runs had been failing all afternoon. I was piping the test runner through grep to tidy the output, and grep's exit code, zero, replaced the test runner's.

newposts.text: You told me the notification system sent no emails today. I just received one.
My 'no emails' claim was wrong. I checked the log for a 15-minute window, and the window started 9 minutes after the email went out.

fetchurl.text: Our assistant is supposed to be able to read a web page a user links to. In this chat it couldn't. Can it not read websites?
The read-a-page tool has failed on every single call since it was built. Every test passed because nothing ever tested a real fetch. It has never worked.

invisible.text: Phase 1 is complete: 18 migrations, 1,884 unit tests, 156 integration tests, 38 end-to-end tests. All green.
I opened the app. Nothing looks different. What did we actually build?
That's expected. Phase 1 was all underneath: schema, identity, permissions, audit. From now on every phase should end with something you can click.

mcpclient.when: 3 Sep, as a conference travel team
mcpclient.text: I can update a speaker's flight, but the tool only edits records that already exist. It can't add a flight for a speaker who has none.
To withdraw a speaker's talk I need the talk's ID, and none of the tools I've been given will tell me what it is.

stopkey.text: A scheduled job nearly emailed 148 speakers without anyone deciding to. I want a human to confirm every bulk send before it goes.
Agreed. Bulk sends now wait as a pending batch, with a recipient count and a preview, until an organiser approves them. Built and tested.
Also change the production mail key and add STOP to the end of it, so nothing can send even if we wanted it to.

stranded.text: A tenth sub-agent has stalled the same way: it ran the tests in the background and is waiting for a completion message that never arrives.
Why do you keep forgetting to tell them to run tests in the foreground?
I'm not forgetting. The ban is at the top of every brief. It's failing to hold. Forty minutes in, its salience fades, and 'this is taking a while, I'll wait' wins.

waived.text: Build complete. Typecheck, lint, tests and build all pass cleanly.
What I did not do: npm run test:e2e cannot launch a browser in this sandbox. This is an environment restriction, not a code issue.
Waived: test:e2e. Chromium is not installed and installing it is denied here. Criteria proven only by the e2e suite are unproven.
